text: Databases store and organise information so we can find it quickly. There are two main types: SQL and NoSQL. SQL databases use tables with rows and columns, while NoSQL databases store data in flexible forms like documents. To get information, we write queries, which are instructions that ask the database questions. Before building a database, we plan its structure through data modeling. This helps us decide what data to keep and how to connect it. We also use indexes to speed up searches, like an index in a book. Good design makes databases fast and reliable.
